title: Right of Return - Revenue Recognition ASC 606
learning_objectives: Account for sales with return rights

content.definition: Customer has right to return product for refund, credit, or exchange within specified period
content.asc_606_treatment: Recognize revenue only for products NOT expected to be returned. Record refund liability for expected returns.

key_accounts.asset_for_right_to_recover: Asset for cost of expected returns (reduce COGS)

accounting_approach.step_1: Estimate expected returns (based on historical data, product type, return period)
accounting_approach.step_2: Recognize revenue only for portion expected to be kept: Revenue = Sales price × (1 - Expected return %)
accounting_approach.step_3: Record refund liability: Liability = Sales price × Expected return %
accounting_approach.step_4: Record asset for products expected to be returned: Asset = Cost × Expected return %

at_sale: CR Refund Liability (expected returns at selling price)
DR Asset - Right to Recover (cost of expected returns)
when_actually_returned: CR AR (or Cash if already collected)

calculation_example.facts: Sell 1,000 units at $100 each (total $100K). Cost $60 per unit (total $60K). Estimate 10% will be returned.
calculation_example.entries: DR AR $100K, CR Revenue $90K, CR Refund Liability $10K. DR COGS $54K, DR Asset $6K, CR Inventory $60K.

actual_returns_differ.if_more_returned: Reduce revenue, increase refund liability (adjustment in period of return)
actual_returns_differ.if_less_returned: Increase revenue, reduce refund liability (when return period expires or becomes remote)
actual_returns_differ.true_up: Adjust estimates as new information available

variable_consideration_constraint.principle: Only recognize revenue to extent probable that significant reversal will NOT occur
variable_consideration_constraint.if_uncertain: If return rate highly uncertain, may need to defer more revenue

exchange_for_similar_product.not_return: Exchange for different product or size = NOT a return (customer keeping something)
exchange_for_similar_product.accounting: Original sale stands, may be separate sale of exchanged item

restocking_fees.revenue_reduction: If customer charged restocking fee, reduces refund liability
restocking_fees.example: 10% restocking fee. Expected return $10K. Net refund = $10K - $1K fee = $9K refund liability.

cpa_exam_tips: Right of return: Recognize revenue only for products NOT expected to be returned
Refund liability = Sales price × Expected return %
Asset for right to recover = Cost × Expected return %
True up estimates when actual returns differ or return period expires
Variable consideration constraint: Only recognize if probable no significant reversal

calculation_steps: 1. Calculate expected return % (given or based on history)
common_mistakes: Recognizing full revenue and later reducing (should recognize net at sale)
Forgetting asset for right to recover (only recording liability)
Not reducing COGS for expected returns (COGS should also be net)

key_points: Right of return: Recognize revenue only for products NOT expected to be returned
Refund liability = Sales price × Expected return %
Asset for right to recover = Cost × Expected return %
True up when actual returns differ from estimate
Variable consideration constraint applies (probable no significant reversal)
